title: Two-Person Invention · Together
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Two-Person Invention · Together with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose two players and a harmless everyday problem. One player proposes an imaginary invention and the partner explains how it helps. The group can identify the problem, the invention and its use. Play eight turns in total, rotating the lead. The group wins together if at least five turns succeed.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: None.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Two-Person Invention, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The group can identify the problem, the invention and its use.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
recall.why: The group can identify the problem, the invention and its use.
